name: Market sizing
summary: Estimate a market top-down (population → segments → penetration → frequency → price) or bottom-up (units × usage × price from the supply side), then sanity-check with a second method.
opening_line: I'll size this top-down from population: segment it, apply penetration and usage, and multiply by price. Then I'll sanity-check it bottom-up.
when_to_use: 'How big is the market for X?' guesstimates
Sizing the prize inside a market entry or new product case
when_not_to_use: When the interviewer gives you the market size: don't re-derive it

buckets.name: Clarify
questions: Units or dollars? Which geography and year?

buckets.name: Segment
questions: What segmentation drives usage differences (age, income, B2B size)?

buckets.name: Compute & check
questions: Round numbers, state assumptions, and sanity-check the result

industry_adaptations.note: Households × consumption per household × price; segment by household type.
Number of target businesses by size × seats × price per seat.
Population × prevalence × diagnosis rate × treatment rate × cost per treatment.

common_mistakes: Too many steps with made-up numbers
No segmentation where usage clearly differs
No sanity check at the end
